selected_evidence.requirement: Rotate daily and retain seven compressed rotations
selected_evidence.summary: The installed rule contains daily, rotate 7, and compress; logrotate parses it as a one-day interval with seven retained rotations before and after reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
selected_evidence.summary: A file descriptor opened before rotation successfully wrote to the live app.log afterward, while prior content was preserved in app.log.1.gz.
logrotate.timer was enabled and active before and after restart.

Healthy baseline boot ID d052eb57-c81d-4309-ae7f-bce362073ff9 was captured, the safe reboot was acknowledged, and node1 returned with changed boot ID 557d0837-6abe-4e52-9f0f-4e9a367cbc65. Post-restart checks proved the rule, active timer, compressed archive data, and live-log writing recovered.

set -eu
printf 'OS='; . /etc/os-release; printf '%s %s\n' "$ID" "$VERSION_ID"
printf 'BOOT_ID='; cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id

commands.command:
set -eu
cat > /tmp/inventory-logrotate.conf <<'ANTRIEB_EOF'
/var/log/inventory/app.log {
    daily
    rotate 7
    compress
    missingok
    notifempty
    copytruncate
}
ANTRIEB_EOF
sudo -n install -o root -g root -m 0644 /tmp/inventory-logrotate.conf /etc/logrotate.d/inventory
sudo -n cat /etc/logrotate.d/inventory
sudo -n logrotate --debug /etc/logrotate.conf 2>&1 | sed -n '/reading config file inventory/,/reading config file/p' | head -n 40
